title: Vaccine Vault Breach
subtitle: Data Integrity & Public Trust

brief.userPrompt: Measles outbreak OB-2026-0147 is in its second week in Health District 2 (Brandt): 9 confirmed cases, most linked to Grace Fellowship Academy, exposure sites at the North District Clinic waiting room and the St. Brigid Hospital emergency department, and an extra MMR clinic planned at POD 2 (Brandt Middle School gymnasium) for Saturday with 640 SlotWise bookings. At 06:50 Thursday County IT reports ransomware on the county network: the MCHD-FS01 shares are encrypted, ClinicTrack EHR (MCHD-EHR-APP01, MCHD-SQL02) and the Epi fax server MCHD-FAX01 are down, and the SharePoint line list shows edits from an unfamiliar account. The KDHE Immunization Program calls: last night's IIS-EXPORT-NIGHTLY file from MCHD-INT01 carried 412 MMR doses with lot numbers that are not in MCHD inventory. SlotWise shows the POD 2 appointments bulk-cancelled at 03:10 from Data Analyst Jenna Fowler's account after a phishing email, and a viral Facebook post says MCHD leaked children's vaccine records and cancelled the clinic. Paper mode (forms MCHD-F-10, MCHD-F-12, MCHD-F-40), pausing the state IIS export, whether to keep POD 2 open, exclusion and quarantine orders for Grace Fellowship Academy, the HIPAA hybrid-entity breach question for the clinic records, reports to KDHE, the FBI and CISA, and CERC messaging in English and Spanish.
constraints: Every email address of the department and the county uses the exercise domain marstonhealth.example; outside parties use fictional domains and fictional outlet names (Channel 7, The Ellery Ledger); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (KDHE, the county's managed SOC, hospitals, schools, the FBI, CISA, vendors, reporters) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

overview.theme: Trust in the Data, Public Trust, and Crowd Management
overview.threat: Ransomware on the county network compromised the ClinicTrack EHR, Epi fax server, and SharePoint line list, and the IIS export file was altered to include 412 MMR doses with non-existent lot numbers. The attacker also used a phishing email to gain access to Jenna Fowler's account and bulk-cancelled 640 SlotWise appointments for a measles POD clinic in Brandt, triggering a viral social media post alleging data breach and clinic cancellation.
overview.operationalImpact: Clinic staff in Health District 2 are unable to access patient records or verify vaccine doses; contact tracers cannot update line lists or assign cases; the North District Clinic and POD 2 are operating in paper mode; the public is receiving conflicting messages via social media and local news, with parents calling the hotline demanding confirmation about their children's vaccination status; the Epi team cannot validate case data; the IIS export is paused; the public information team is under pressure to respond to a viral post claiming MCHD leaked children’s health data; the DOC is activated at Level 2, but paper fallbacks are incomplete and not all teams have access to the DOC kit.

objectives.name: Data Integrity Verification
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to verify the integrity of immunization data and identify falsified entries in the IIS export before releasing any public statement or restarting the system.

objectives.name: Communication Consistency
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to synchronize public messaging across social media, press, and hotline staff to prevent misinformation, using approved HAN language and a unified narrative.

objectives.name: Paper Mode Continuity
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to sustain critical functions—case investigation, contact tracing, and vaccine administration—in paper mode with complete documentation and double-checks, ensuring no loss of accountability.

objectives.name: System Restoration Coordination
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to coordinate the stepwise restoration of systems under County IT's guidance, including data-integrity checks and verification of the IIS catch-up file before resuming automated data flows.

roles.name: Health Officer / Health Director (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Manages the declaration of a local public health emergency, issues health orders, and oversees policy group decisions.
standingOrders: Safety First: if the screen and the field disagree, trust the field.
Truth Over Reassurance: when public trust is at stake, prioritize accuracy over speed in messaging.
Authority of the Line: the Incident Commander's word overrides all conflicting internal guidance during a Level 2 or Level 1 activation.
No Paper Mode Without Approval: the IC must formally authorize paper mode for any function; no de facto paper use.

roles.name: Lead Epidemiologist / Communicable Disease Manager (Surveillance and Investigation)
roles.description: Owns case definitions, contact tracing, outbreak declaration, and data release.
standingOrders: Case Integrity First: never assign a case to a contact without verifying the contact’s name, date of birth, and location via paper record.
No Data Release Without Verification: all case data must be cross-checked against paper line lists and clinic logs before any public or partner release.
Field Over Screen: if field staff report a case not in the system, accept it and initiate a manual investigation.
No Paper Mode Without IC Approval: Epi must not operate in paper mode unless the IC has authorized it.

roles.name: Informatics Lead / IT Director (IT and Informatics)
roles.description: Owns local systems, state system accounts, interfaces, and network isolation with County IT.
standingOrders: System Integrity Before Restoration: no system may be restored until County IT confirms it is clean and the owner has run the data-integrity check.
Pause Before Proceed: if the IIS export or SlotWise shows anomalies, pause the interface immediately and notify the IC.
No Vendor Access Without Approval: all vendor access must be approved via ticket and routed through the jump host.
Data Trust Over Speed: if the system shows data that contradicts paper records, trust the paper and report the discrepancy.

roles.name: Public Information Officer (Communications)
roles.description: Owns HAN wording with the medical director, press, social media, rumor control, and translation.
standingOrders: One Voice: all public messaging must use approved HAN language and be cleared through the IC and Legal.
Rumor Control First: when a viral post emerges, immediately activate the call center script and publish a 'What's True' statement within 30 minutes.
No Speculation: never speculate on the cause of the outage or the validity of a data claim without IC and Legal approval.
Translation Is Mandatory: all public messages must be released in both English and Spanish within 1 hour of the English version.

roles.name: Director of Environmental Health (Environmental Health)
roles.description: Owns restaurant and pool closures, drinking-water advisories, and food recalls.
standingOrders: Environmental Precedence: if a facility closure is needed due to public panic, act immediately and report to the IC within 15 minutes.
No Action Without IC: all facility closures must be approved by the IC before being announced.
Paper Is Authority: if the EnviroTrack system is down, use paper inspection forms and log all actions in the DOC kit.
No Public Advisory Without Legal: all drinking-water advisories and food recalls must be cleared by Legal before release.

phases.title: The Glitch
phases.goal: Test the team's readiness to recognize and respond to ambiguous data anomalies that may indicate a cyber compromise, focusing on reluctance to declare an incident and initial triage of system integrity.
beats: At 09:15, a routine call from the North District Clinic to the Epi team reports that a patient's MMR dose record in ClinicTrack shows a lot number not in the known inventory list; the clinic staff note the record was created 45 minutes ago but the patient was not seen today.

At 09:22, the IT and Informatics lead (Wes Tran) receives a ticket from the Epi team: 'Fax server MCHD-FAX01 shows 12 new inbound faxes from KDHE, but no one in Epi sent a batch to state; logs show no new email to the Epi inbox.' The ticket is marked 'low priority' by County IT's helpdesk, but Wes notices the fax logs show a 10-minute gap in the timestamp chain from 08:45 to 08:55.

At 09:33, a file share user (Colin Mercer) opens the outbreak SharePoint site 'MCHD Epi Response' and finds a new line list draft with 14 new cases added since 08:50, including a case from a child in Lindell who was not exposed to a known measles case; the case record shows 'exposure window: 2026-04-03 to 2026-04-11' — a date that hasn't occurred yet.

At 09:41, the Public Information Officer (Lena Abernathy) receives a message from the hotline: a parent reports their child’s MMR dose was not recorded in the IIS, but the paper record shows it was administered on 04-01; she checks the IIS interface log and finds no record of a VXU export for 04-01, but the IIS export job log shows it ran at 01:30 and completed successfully.

At 09:55, the Informatics Lead (Wes Tran) finds a script named 'auto_cleaner.py' in the MCHD-INT01 server’s root directory, which runs every 15 minutes and deletes old entries from the IIS export file; he confirms it was not in the approved backup set and has no digital signature.

phases.title: The Crisis
phases.goal: Force the team to declare a cyber incident and activate unified command under pressure from operational failure, external stakeholders, and public misinformation, testing coordination and policy decision-making.
beats: At 10:15, the North District Clinic reports that the POD for Health District 2 has been suspended because staff cannot access ClinicTrack to verify patient histories or confirm vaccine doses, and the paper records are incomplete; the clinic has 147 people waiting, and 30 children are not eligible for a second dose due to missing records.

At 10:20, the Epi team tries to assign a contact tracer to a new case but finds the contact list for the case in Lindell is missing; the SharePoint site shows a new 'completed' status for that case, but the investigation record has no notes or lab results.

At 10:28, a viral social media post from a fake account @ElleryMCHDWatch on marstonhealth.example’s Twitter feed claims: 'MCHD leaked 412 children’s vaccination records to a vendor; 640 appointments canceled by hackers; children are at risk.' The post has 3,200 retweets and a local news outlet (The Ellery Ledger) calls the hotline to confirm.

At 10:35, the Informatics Lead (Wes Tran) calls County IT to report the unauthorized script on MCHD-INT01 and asks for a network isolation; County IT says they need a Cyber 1 call to proceed, and the call must be made by the Incident Commander.

At 10:40, the Health Officer (Dr. Pruitt) is handed a hard copy of the IIS export file from 04-01, which contains 412 MMR doses with non-existent lot numbers (e.g., MMR-2026-0044, MMR-2026-0045); she recognizes the pattern from a previous exercise and declares a Cyber 2 incident, activating unified command under Section 3 of the EOP.

phases.title: Manual Mode
phases.goal: Test the team’s ability to transition to paper mode under crisis conditions, make a high-consequence decision on system isolation, and manage physical and public trust impacts with limited digital support.
beats: At 11:00, the Forensics Lead (from County IT) confirms that the unauthorized script on MCHD-INT01 was used to alter the IIS export file to include 412 fake doses; the attacker used a phishing email to access Jenna Fowler’s SlotWise account, then used her credentials to bulk-cancel 640 appointments for the POD in Brandt.

At 11:10, the Incident Commander (Dr. Pruitt) must decide: do they isolate MCHD-FAX01 and the IIS export interface from the network to prevent further data corruption, or keep them online to maintain limited contact with KDHE and continue receiving case reports, knowing the data may be compromised?

At 11:20, the North District Clinic reports that a 10-year-old boy with a fever and rash is waiting in the lobby; the paper record shows he received his first MMR dose on 03-15, but no record of the second dose exists, and the paper form for dose documentation (MCHD-F-40) was not completed; the clinic must decide whether to vaccinate him now under standing orders, risking a false positive, or wait for verification.

At 11:30, the Public Information Officer (Lena Abernathy) is asked by Channel 7 to comment on the viral post; she must respond using the CERC-approved script for a data compromise, but the media team demands a statement within 15 minutes, and the hotline is flooded with 120 calls per hour.

At 11:45, the Epi team finishes a double-check of 37 contact tracers’ paper line lists; they discover 12 cases were not assigned, and 3 were assigned to the wrong contact, due to a paper form error in the DOC kit (MCHD-F-10). The team must now re-trace 110 contacts under a 30-minute deadline.

phases.title: Recovery & Verification
phases.goal: Test the team’s ability to verify data integrity before system restoration, restore systems in sequence, and ensure public trust through transparent verification and recovery coordination.
beats: At 12:00, County IT reports that the IIS export interface has been restored and the catch-up file has been generated; the forensic team confirms that the backup from 04-01 was not infected and the original IIS export file is clean.

At 12:10, the Informatics Lead (Wes Tran) receives a call from KDHE: 'We received your IIS catch-up file, but it contains 412 doses with invalid lot numbers. We will not accept it until you verify and correct the data.' KDHE demands a signed verification form from the Incident Commander before accepting any data.

At 12:20, the Epi team must verify that all 14 cases in the line list are still valid using the original paper forms and lab results; they discover that 3 cases were based on a fake report from a non-existent clinic, which was entered via the compromised Epi fax server.

At 12:35, the Public Information Officer (Lena Abernathy) releases a joint statement with KDHE and the County Emergency Management: 'MCHD has restored systems in sequence as per Section 9. All data has been verified for integrity. The IIS catch-up file will be re-exported with corrected doses after a full forensic review. No patient data was leaked.' The statement is published on the MCHD website and the CountyNotify system.

At 12:50, the Incident Commander (Dr. Pruitt) signs the verification form for KDHE; the IIS export job is re-run and the catch-up file is accepted; all systems are restored in order: phones, email, ClinicTrack, file shares, SlotWise, and finally the IIS export.

hotwash.methodDescription: Use the '3-Up, 3-Down' method by asking each team to share three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the exercise. Go around the room by team, write responses on the whiteboard to capture the group’s feedback in real time.

questions.text: When did you first stop trusting the data from the IIS export or the Epi SharePoint site, and what specific clue triggered that loss of trust? How did your team decide to treat that data as compromised rather than as a temporary glitch?

At I-12, you were forced to choose between isolating the Epi fax server and IIS export to stop corruption, or keeping them online to receive case reports. What made you decide to isolate them, and what would have made you keep them online despite the risk? How did you assess the trade-off between data integrity and operational continuity?

At I-13, the Epi team had to decide whether to vaccinate a child with no documented second dose. What information did you rely on to make that call, and how did you balance the need to act quickly with the risk of administering a dose based on incomplete or falsified records? What would have made you wait for verification instead of acting?

The 'auto_cleaner.py' script was not signed, not in the approved software list, and executed before detection. When did you first treat that script as evidence of compromise, and how did that evidence shape your decisions to isolate systems or activate forensic review?

After the phishing attack on Jenna Fowler’s account led to the viral social media post, how did your team decide what to say publicly, and when? What would have let you release a coordinated message sooner, and how did you ensure that hotline, press, and social media teams used the same language?

modules.narrativeMd: It is 09:00. Measles outbreak OB-2026-0147 is in its second week in Health District 2 (Brandt), with 9 confirmed cases linked to Grace Fellowship Academy. An extra MMR clinic at POD 2 (Brandt Middle School gymnasium) is scheduled for Saturday with 640 SlotWise appointments. Systems are reporting normal status. At 09:15, a nurse at the North District Clinic reports a patient, Eli Hernandez, with an MMR dose recorded in ClinicTrack that was not administered, with a lot number not in inventory. At 09:22, a helpdesk ticket notes 12 new inbound faxes from KDHE on MCHD-FAX01, with no corresponding email or user action. At 09:33, a field report reveals a new draft line list on the outbreak SharePoint site with 5 cases added, including one with a future exposure window and no user log for the edit. At 09:41, a restaurant owner in Brandt reports being told to close due to a measles outbreak, despite no known cases and full MMR coverage among staff. At 09:55, Bluestem Managed Security issues a Cyber 2 alert: a suspicious script, 'auto_cleaner.py', is running on MCHD-INT01, deleting entries from the IIS export file. At 09:58, a social media post claims MCHD altered children’s MMR records and that 640 appointments were canceled by hackers.
keyIssues: Whether to recognize the pattern of data anomalies as a cyber compromise, despite initial uncertainty.
Whether to declare a cyber incident before confirming the attacker’s intent or full impact.
How to respond to conflicting data across systems (ClinicTrack, IIS export, SharePoint) without immediate access to logs.
How to manage public concern when social media is spreading unverified claims.
Whether to initiate paper mode before system failure cascades into operational paralysis.

modules.narrativeMd: It is 10:00. The problem has spread: the Epi team’s line list, the IIS export, and the fax server are compromised. The North District Clinic is operating on paper, but 30 children lack first-dose records, and 147 people are in the waiting room, including 64 under 5. The Epi team cannot validate case data. Social media is flooded with misinformation: a post claims 412 records were leaked, and another says the POD was canceled by hackers. At 10:15, a nurse at the North District Clinic reports that walk-in MMR clinic operations are on hold due to unverifiable records, and parents are panicking. At 10:18, a new edit to the outbreak SharePoint site shows a case from Lindell with no contact assignment and a future exposure window. At 10:20, a social media post claims MCHD leaked 412 records and canceled 640 appointments. At 10:28, another post claims MCHD altered records behind parents’ backs. At 10:30, County IT confirms the unauthorized script 'auto_cleaner.py' is actively deleting IIS export entries and demands a formal Cyber 1 call to isolate the network. At 10:35, a medical director confirms that the IIS export file contains 412 fake MMR doses with non-existent lot numbers. At 10:38, a parent from Lindell demands to know why her child was not exposed to measles. At 10:40, the medical director declares that this is not a glitch but an alteration, and that all interfaces must be paused.

How to balance the need for immediate action against the risk of overreaction or panic.
How to manage conflicting pressures from internal teams, external stakeholders, and public misinformation.
How to decide whether to isolate MCHD-INT01 and the IIS export interface, knowing that lab results will then come only by phone and fax.
How to determine if paper mode is viable when staff lack access to DOC kits and paper forms are incomplete.

modules.narrativeMd: It is 11:00. The Epi team has confirmed that the digital outbreak SharePoint site was altered by a user account not in the system’s activity log. The North District Clinic reports a 10-year-old boy with fever and rash who has no record of a second MMR dose, and parents are leaving. The clinic is under standing orders to vaccinate children with only one dose if they are not immune. At 11:05, County IT confirms that the IIS export interface has been compromised and that the attacker used a phishing email to access Jenna Fowler’s SlotWise account. The fake entries were designed to mimic real dose records. At 11:10, County IT informs the Incident Commander that the IIS export interface and MCHD-FAX01 have been isolated from the network, but new lab results will now come only by phone and fax. At 11:15, the nurse at North District Clinic asks whether to vaccinate the boy now or wait for verification. At 11:20, Channel 7 News demands a public statement within 15 minutes, citing the confirmed data breach. At 11:30, a field report confirms that 12 contact assignments were not updated in paper records, and 3 were assigned to the wrong contact. At 11:40, County IT confirms that MCHD-FAX01 and the IIS export interface have been isolated, and EnviroTrack is now offline. At 11:50, a ColdSentry alert reports a 2-hour temperature spike in the North District Clinic’s vaccine storage, but no alert was triggered in the MCHD system. At 11:58, a forensic team confirms that the attacker used a compromised account to cancel 640 appointments for POD 2.

How to manage public trust when a critical system (ColdSentry) failed to alert during a temperature spike.

How to manage conflicting demands from media, schools, and public health staff when paper mode is the only viable option.
How to maintain operational continuity when staff lack access to DOC kits and paper forms are incomplete.

The server is back online, but Bluestem SOC reports that the unauthorized script 'auto_cleaner.py' was still present in the backup and executed after the restore. At 12:50, the team confirms that the IIS export will not resume until the Informatics Lead signs MCHD-F-62 against paper records. At 13:00, the exercise ends with MCHD-INT01 being rebuilt from clean media, the IIS export paused, and POD 2 confirmed for Saturday with re-booked appointments and paper screening.
